title: Adding and Subtracting Fractions and Mixed Numbers
seo_title: Year 7 Adding and Subtracting Fractions Worksheets: Common Denominators and Mixed Numbers
standard_text: Use the four operations, including formal written methods, applied to integers, decimals, proper and improper fractions, and mixed numbers, all both positive and negative.
meta_desc: Free Year 7 worksheets on adding and subtracting fractions: same and different denominators, finding a common denominator, mixed numbers and word problems. 100 questions with step-by-step answers.
key_big: Make the denominators the same, then add or subtract the numerators. Never add the denominators.
key_sub: Use the LCM of the denominators as the common denominator, and simplify your answer.
body_html:
How it works

You can only add or subtract fractions when the denominators are the same. Then add or subtract the numerators and keep the denominator.

If the denominators are different, find a common denominator (the LCM of the denominators) and make equivalent fractions first. Always simplify your answer.

Example

Work out 2/3 + 1/4.

The LCM of 3 and 4 is 12.

2/3 = 8/12 and 1/4 = 3/12.

8/12 + 3/12 = 11/12.

Answer: 11/12

Example

Work out 3 1/4 − 1 2/3.

Improper fractions: 13/4 − 5/3.

Common denominator 12: 39/12 − 20/12 = 19/12.

Answer: 1 7/12

Common mistakes

  • Adding the denominators: 1/3 + 1/4 is not 2/7.
  • Changing the denominator but not the numerator: 1/2 is 2/4, not 1/4.
  • Forgetting to simplify: 6/8 should be 3/4.
  • With mixed numbers, taking the smaller fraction from the bigger one: 3 1/4 − 1 2/3 is not 2 5/12.

faq.q: How do you add fractions with different denominators?
faq.a: Find a common denominator, usually the LCM. Change both fractions to that denominator, then add the numerators.

faq.q: Why can't I add the denominators?
faq.a: The denominator tells you the size of the pieces. 1/3 + 1/4 are different sized pieces, so first cut them into twelfths.

faq.q: How do I subtract mixed numbers?
faq.a: Either change them to improper fractions first, or subtract the whole numbers and the fractions separately, exchanging a whole if the first fraction is smaller.

faq.q: Do I always need to simplify?
faq.a: Yes. Give the final answer in its simplest form, and as a mixed number if it is more than 1.
